title: Auqib Nabi Joins Surrey for Three County Games Ahead of India's New Zealand Test Tour
excerpt: The Jammu and Kashmir pacer, India's leading domestic wicket-taker, will play three Division One fixtures as the BCCI prepares him for November's Test series in New Zealand.
body:
• Jammu and Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi has signed a short-term deal with Surrey for three County Championship Division One fixtures, starting September 2 against Yorkshire at The Oval.
  • The BCCI arranged the stint to give Nabi red-ball experience in swing-friendly English conditions ahead of India's two-Test tour of New Zealand in November.
  • Nabi was India's standout domestic bowler in 2025-26, taking 60 Ranji Trophy wickets at 12.56 and leading J&K to their maiden championship title.
  • He joins fellow Indian players Rahul Chahar and Mahipal Lomror at Surrey, as multiple Indian cricketers gain county exposure this English summer.

Jammu and Kashmir fast bowler Auqib Nabi is headed to England for a three-match stint with Surrey in the County Championship Division One, a move orchestrated by the BCCI to sharpen his red-ball skills before India's Test tour of New Zealand later this year.

Nabi received his UK work visa clearance on Saturday and boarded the first available flight from New Delhi on Sunday, according to ESPNcricinfo and IANS. He is expected to be available for Surrey's fixture against Yorkshire, starting September 2 at The Oval.

From Ranji Hero to County Prospect

The 29-year-old seamer has had a breakout year. He finished as the leading wicket-taker in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season with 60 wickets at an average of 12.56, delivering seven five-wicket hauls including one in the final against Karnataka. His efforts powered J&K to their historic maiden Ranji Trophy title in March — a landmark moment for cricket in the region.

Across two consecutive Ranji seasons, Nabi has taken 104 wickets, placing him among the most productive pace bowlers in Indian domestic cricket. Those numbers earned him a call-up to India's Test squad for the home series against Sri Lanka earlier this month as a replacement for Jasprit Bumrah, who failed to get a fitness clearance.

However, Nabi did not feature in either Test as India opted to field Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna as their frontline seamers in the series, which the hosts won 1-0.

Preparing for New Zealand Conditions

With India's two-Test tour of New Zealand scheduled for November, the team management and selectors felt Nabi would benefit from bowling in conditions that demand swing and seam movement with the red Kookaburra ball.

"The main purpose of this stint is for the Indian team management and selectors to check if Nabi can swing the ball well there in England, as the climate in New Zealand for the Test series will need for him to do that in conducive conditions."

— A source familiar with the development, to IANS

Nabi is expected to feature in three remaining Division One fixtures: against Yorkshire (September 2, The Oval), Sussex (September 8, Hove), and Glamorgan (September 15, The Oval). He is expected to return to India in time for India A's four-day fixtures against Australia A in Puducherry, starting September 22.

Indian Contingent in County Cricket

Nabi joins a growing Indian presence in English county cricket this summer. Surrey already have India leg-spinner Rahul Chahar and uncapped batting all-rounder Mahipal Lomror in their squad. Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar, who picked 16 wickets during the Sri Lanka Tests, is rejoining Warwickshire, while left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav will return to Yorkshire.

The BCCI has increasingly used county stints as preparation tools for overseas tours, with players gaining valuable experience in English conditions that closely mirror those in New Zealand, Australia, and South Africa.

What's Next for Nabi

Beyond the county stint, Nabi's schedule is packed. The J&K selectors are waiting to hear from the national selectors before picking their squad for the Irani Cup, which takes place October 1-5 in Srinagar. Since the second India A vs Australia A fixture clashes with the Irani Cup, the selectors will need to balance their squads, with Nabi expected to play for one of the teams.

For now, the immediate task is clear: prove he can move the red ball in English conditions and make an irresistible case for a spot in India's New Zealand-bound Test squad.
